title: Pruned-range fetch with no full-history peer
severity_reason: Every pruned-range request fails: 7 of 7 return lgrNotFound. The 4 first attempts each burn 7 acquire timeouts (21 s); the 3 repeats of the failed candidate hash short-circuit on the failed-hash cache (0 ms). Total wasted acquire time 84,000 ms. The data is unrecoverable from the available peer set.

title: Partial-history node: backfill stops at the 256 window
severity_reason: The background backfill refuses to fetch anything below the 256-ledger window even though a full-history peer holds it, while on-demand RPC fetches the same ledgers successfully. Stored history never grows past the window; every deep lookup is a live peer fetch.

title: Backfill from a pruned peer stalls at the peer boundary
severity_reason: Backfill recovers 742 ledgers down to the peer's prune boundary (1258), then the floor ledger 1257 fails after 7 acquire timeouts (21 s) because no peer holds it. Everything below the online-delete floor is never attempted by design, so the node's history stops at 1258 with a one-ledger gap at the floor.

title: LedgerCleaner repair depends on peer availability
severity_reason: Repair succeeds for every ledger a peer holds (3 of 4: one recovered from the peer, one with a re-saved SQL row), and fails for the one ledger no peer holds (1000), which is dropped from the complete set. A pruned ledger with no full peer cannot be repaired.

title: Fetch-depth clamp and the fetch-pack earliest gate
severity_reason: A fetch-pack root below getEarliestFetch is refused with feeMalformedRequest, and the clamp means online_delete (256) binds before fetch_depth does at the default. With fetch_depth narrowed to 100, the earliest fetch rises to 1900 and two more roots are refused.

title: Aggressive pruning: online_delete 256 over 600 ledgers
severity_reason: Pruning deletes exactly as configured and the node keeps serving every requested ledger because a full-history peer exists. The availability cost appears only when no such peer exists (see S2).

title: Rotation deferred while stale or syncing, then catches up
severity_reason: Rotation is deferred for 300 ledgers while the validated age is 61 s (above the 60 s threshold) and for 10 more while the node is syncing, then fires on the first close after the node is healthy again. No data is lost beyond the configured interval.

title: Backfill with a full-history second peer
severity_reason: With a full-history peer available, the backfill reaches the online-delete floor (1257) and stops there: 743 ledgers acquired. The floor, not peer availability, is the binding constraint.

title: Advisory can_delete: never, hash, now, always
severity_reason: Advisory delete works exactly as documented: 'never' blocks rotation entirely, a hash authorises up to that ledger, 'now' authorises exactly one more rotation (the gate is can_delete >= lastRotated - 1), and 'always' releases every later rotation.

title: RPC ledger resolution matrix (index, hash, age, version)
severity_reason: Every documented branch resolves as coded, with one asymmetry worth knowing: hash requests bypass the validated-age gate that index requests hit, so a stale node still serves hash lookups while index lookups return rpcNOT_SYNCED.

title: Baseline: full-history node, no pruning
severity_reason: Control case. No pruning configured, so every ledger in the modelled chain is served locally.
